items.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: So I all of a sudden started hearing musicians like Don Byas and Eddie Miller and Mary Lou Williams and Bill Coleman

ctx.x: A moldy fig. I haven’t heard that term in a while.

That was an old term. Yeah. The figs and the boppers in those days. But at that time I had never heard of bebop. I had a pretty good jazz collection. I collected everything from Duke Ellington, of course, the big bands that were popular in those days. I collected jazz just because it was pop music. I was collecting Benny Goodman, Harry James, Tommy Dorsey, Glenn Miller, all that stuff. But by some wonderful fluke, this little electric store that sold stoves and refrigerators in Kirkland, Washington, had a little…
Wasn’t in the pile, that’s all.
